proposals.before: Corvée labor was restored for descendants of the Kong clan and for descendants of the main lines of Yan and Meng.
proposals.after: Corvée labor was remitted for descendants of the Kong clan and for descendants of the main lines of Yan and Meng.
proposals.reason: 復徭役 here means restoration of exemption from corvée, matching the idiomatic lifting of obligations, not reinstatement of labor duties.

proposals.before: The emperor was pleased and that same day promoted him to Junior Mentor to lecture the heir apparent.
proposals.after: The emperor was pleased and that same day specially promoted both men to Junior Mentor to lecture and read with the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 同日超拜少詹事 follows a recommendation of both Gongxun and Sima Xun; the singular 'him' omits Sima Xun and understates 超拜.

proposals.before: The emperor was pleased and on the same day promoted him to Junior Mentor, to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
proposals.after: The emperor was pleased and on the same day specially promoted both men to Junior Mentor, to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
proposals.reason: Same omission of the dual promotion of Gongxun and Sima Xun.

proposals.before: In the sixth year bandits broke out in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang proposed fortifying Qufu and moving the county seat to protect the temple, but the plan was never carried out.
proposals.after: In the sixth year bandits broke out in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang proposed fortifying Queli and moving the Qufu county seat to protect the temple, but the plan was never carried out.
proposals.reason: Chinese 城闕里 means walling Queli, not fortifying Qufu; 遷曲阜縣治 is the separate proposal to move the county seat.

proposals.before: Kong Yanchang, whose courtesy name was Chaowu, was from Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
proposals.after: Kong Yansheng, whose courtesy name was Chaowu, was from Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
proposals.reason: 彥繩 is Yansheng; 繩 is sheng, not chang.

proposals.before: Kong Yanchang, courtesy name Chaowu, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
proposals.after: Kong Yansheng, courtesy name Chaowu, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
proposals.reason: The literal English repeats the 彥繩 romanization error.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Wanli his stepmother, the Guo clan, accused Shangxian.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Wanli his stepmother née Guo accused Shangxian.
proposals.reason: 郭氏 names a woman of the Guo surname, not the Guo clan as accuser.

proposals.before: Soon afterward, because Xihui was not born of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was reappointed instead.
proposals.after: Soon afterward, because Xihui was not born of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was appointed instead.
proposals.reason: 仍以 marks substituting Yi for Xihui in the doctorate, not a second appointment of Yi, who had not previously held the post.

proposals.before: Before long, because Xihui was not the son of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was again appointed.
proposals.after: Before long, because Xihui was not the son of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was then appointed.
proposals.reason: 仍以 does not mean Yi was appointed again; it assigns the post to Xiren's eldest son after Xihui is rejected as not a principal-wife son.

proposals.before: Thereupon the Jiangxi grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner reported Zhicui's name; he was ordered to return to Jiaxiang and perform sacrifices in ordinary dress.
proposals.after: Thereupon the Jiangxi grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner reported Zhicui's name; he was ordered to return to Jiaxiang and perform sacrifices in scholar's dress.
proposals.reason: 衣巾 denotes the scholar's robe and kerchief used for sacrificial service, not ordinary civilian clothing.

proposals.before: Hao's son Jizu, styled Shengzhi, had been partly blind from youth; a Jiangxi kinsman named Gun tried to seize the post but was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was removed from office and Jizu retained charge of the sacrifices.
proposals.after: Hao's son Jizu, styled Shengzhi, had suffered from eye disease from youth; a Jiangxi kinsman named Gun tried to seize the post but was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was removed from office and Jizu retained charge of the sacrifices.
proposals.reason: 少病目 records eye illness from youth, not a demonstrated partial loss of sight.
Chinese 呂子銓 is a genealogical formula 'Lü's son was Quan', not a compound personal name Lü Ziquan.
The literal English likewise fuses father and son into one invented compound name.

proposals.before: In Chongzhen 16, on Duke Yinzhi's recommendation, an edict made Yubi Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, and granted more than sixty qing of land in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture plus thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.
proposals.after: In Chongzhen 16, on the recommendation of Kong Yinzhi, Duke of Yan Sheng, an edict made Yubi Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, and granted more than sixty qing of land in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture plus thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the surname Kong and the title 衍聖公, leaving an opaque 'Duke Yinzhi'.

proposals.before: Zhu Ting, styled Mengling, was a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi and his family had long lived at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.
proposals.after: Zhu Ting, styled Mengling, was a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi. His family had long lived at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世居 attaches to Zhu Ting's line, not to Zhu Xi; the coordinated 'and his family' can be read as Zhu Xi's household.

decisions.reason: 復…徭役 here is a privilege of exemption (復除), matching the surrounding honors for the Kong, Yan, and Meng lines; “restored” would reinstate labor duties and reverse the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 復孔氏子孫及顏、孟大宗子孫徭役

decisions.reason: 李賢 recommended both 公恂 and 司馬恂; 同日超拜少詹事 and 聖賢子孫為汝子傅 show a same-day leap promotion of both men to lecture and read for the heir, not a singular “him.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝喜，同日超拜少詹事，侍東宮講讀

decisions.reason: The same sentence promotes both men named in the preceding memorial; 超拜 is a special leap appointment omitted by “promoted him.”
城闕里 is a proposal to wall Queli; 遷曲阜縣治 is a separate move of the Qufu county seat. Fortifying “Qufu” collapses the two places.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 請城闕里，遷曲阜縣治以衛廟

decisions.reason: 彥繩 romanizes as Yansheng; 繩 is shéng, not cháng. “Yanchang” is a naming error.
The literal field repeats the same 彥繩 romanization error as the idiomatic sentence.
庶母郭氏 is Shangxian’s stepmother, a woman née Guo; the appositive “the Guo clan” makes the clan the accuser.
After 希惠 is rejected as 非嫡子, 仍以希仁長子議為之 assigns the doctorate to Yi for the first time; “reappointed” invents a prior tenure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以希惠非嫡子，仍以希仁長子議為之

decisions.reason: 仍以 marks filling the post with Xiren’s eldest son after Xihui, not a second appointment of Yi.
衣巾 is the scholar’s robe and kerchief for sacrificial service, not ordinary civilian dress.
少病目 records eye illness from youth; “partly blind” adds a degree of sight loss the Chinese does not state.
呂子銓 is the same father–son formula as 銓子則顯 and 則顯子於陛, not a compound name Lü Ziquan.
The literal English likewise fuses 呂 and his son 銓 into one invented personal name.
The source names 衍聖公孔蔭植; “Duke Yinzhi” drops both the Kong surname and the Yan Sheng dukedom.
世居 follows 朱梴…九世孫也 and describes Ting’s line at 紫霞洲, not Zhu Xi’s household; the coordinated “and his family” can attach to Zhu Xi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 先賢文公朱子九世孫也，世居福建建安縣之紫霞洲

claimRetractions.reason: “Duke Yinzhi” is an English fusion of 衍聖公 and the given name 蔭植; the source supports Kong Yinzhi holding the title Duke of Yan Sheng, already captured in other claims, not a title “Duke Yinzhi.”

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name must follow 彥繩 as Yansheng, not Yanchang.
The given-name English value repeats the same 繩/sheng error.
